critiques.description: The mapping asserts that req-TPI-001 is "partially_satisfied" for the managed vector database, but the cited evidence only establishes that a third-party service is used and that an internal ingestion pipeline governs what is written, not that any third-party retention, usage, or security commitments are in place.
critiques.rationale: map-015 links req-TPI-001 to thr-005 and classifies it as applicable and "partially_satisfied," citing evd-002 and evd-012 and control ctl-003. evd-002 and evd-012 document that embeddings of resolved support tickets are stored in a managed vector database operated by an external provider and that this index is the only copy of the embeddings, reachable from the answer service's network segment, with a nightly ingestion pipeline as the sole writer from named sources. None of these passages describe the managed provider's retention period, backup handling, or data-usage terms for the embeddings, nor any contractual or platform guarantees about how the provider processes customer data. ctl-003 governs the ingestion pipeline and the sources of data, not the third-party provider's handling of stored embeddings. In parallel, gap-009 explicitly notes that the absence of provider retention/usage documentation prevents determining whether external-processor expectations in req-TPI-001 are met for this index. Taken together, the available evidence supports applicability of req-TPI-001 but does not support a conclusion that it is already partially satisfied for this threat; that status appears inferred without documented provider commitments.
